$comment: Known RLS findings accepted as TRACKED DEBT so CI is green while they are
scheduled for remediation. This is a to-do list, NOT a permanent exemption:
the linter fails on anything NOT listed here, and warns when a listed entry
no longer matches (meaning it was fixed and should be deleted from this file).
All four entries are the same bug class as SEC-1 finding F-2: a write policy
with USING but no WITH CHECK. PostgreSQL reuses USING as WITH CHECK, which
constrains row ownership but not column values.
Discovered by scripts/security/check-migrations.mjs on its first run (SEC-3).
Full analysis and proposed fixes: docs/security/sec-3-devsecops.md section 5.

001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::profiles_update.why_still_listed: The linter analyses each migration file in isolation and cannot know that a later migration redefines the policy. This entry documents that limitation; do not remove it while 001 remains in history.

001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::enrollments_upd.risk: A learner may UPDATE their own enrollment row with no column constraint (e.g. status, expiry).
001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::enrollments_upd.impact_today: Low — pilot mode grants free enrollment anyway, so there is nothing to gain.
001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::enrollments_upd.impact_later: Access-control bypass once enrollment is paid or time-limited.
001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::enrollments_upd.proposed_fix: Add WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid() AND status IS NOT DISTINCT FROM <current>), or drop the learner UPDATE policy entirely — enrollment writes go through service-role server actions.

001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::payments_update.why_still_listed: The linter analyses each migration in isolation and cannot know that a later migration drops the policy. This entry documents that limitation, exactly as profiles_update_own does for 027; do not remove it while 001 remains in history.
001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::payments_update.risk: WAS: a learner could run UPDATE payments SET status='completed' WHERE user_id = auth.uid(). payments.status is CHECK-constrained to a value list that includes 'completed', so the write was accepted.
001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::payments_update.fix_applied: 058 closes BOTH layers, because dropping the policy alone would have left the privilege. (a) It drops payments_update_own AND the FOR ALL payments_admin_all, and adds RESTRICTIVE deny policies for UPDATE and DELETE so no permissive policy added later can re-open them. (b) It revokes every privilege except SELECT from anon and authenticated — Supabase's default grants had given both roles table-wide INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, which no policy change removes. Learner and admin READ are preserved through payments_own; service_role keeps everything, which is what both admin surfaces and the PAY-2 webhook act through.
001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::payments_update.apply_state: 058 is NOT YET APPLIED to production. Until it is, the risk above is still live in the database — but payments remain inactive (PLATFORM_MODE=pilot, NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYMENTS_ENABLED unset) and production holds ZERO payment rows.
001_phase_a_rls_fix.sql::payments_update.regression_tests: __tests__/payments/pay-launch-02b-payment-foundation.test.ts (source invariants) plus the offline PGlite harness (behaviour, three corpora, 22 mutants).

018_certificates_pdf_bucket.sql::cert_se.risk: Scoped only by bucket_id, with no per-user folder restriction (unlike the sibling SELECT policy, which scopes to (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()). Any authenticated user may therefore update ANY object in the certificates bucket.
018_certificates_pdf_bucket.sql::cert_se.proposed_fix: Restrict to the owner's folder and add a matching WITH CHECK, mirroring the SELECT policy, or limit the policy to the service role.
